studies.Reference: Long-term alcohol consumption and risk of endometrial cancer incidence: a prospective cohort study.
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Alcohol consumption was assessed with validated food frequency questionnaires at baseline 1987 to 1990 and at follow-up in 1997.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: We used data from the prospective population-based Swedish Mammography Cohort including 61,226 women.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The multivariable rate ratios (95% confidence intervals) for the three upper categories of long-term alcohol consumption as compared with no consumption were ... 1.09 (0.71-1.67) for >or=10 g/d.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: We found no association between alcohol consumption and endometrial cancer risk after adjustment for age, body mass index, and smoking.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: During a mean follow-up of 17.6 years, 687 endometrial cancer cases were identified in the Swedish cancer registries.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol consumption was assessed with validated food frequency questionnaires at baseline 1987 to 1990 and at follow-up in 1997.

studies.Reference: Alcohol consumption and postmenopausal endometrial cancer: results from the Iowa Women's Health Study.
studies.Authors: Gapstur SM, Potter JD, Sellers TA, Kushi LH, Folsom AR
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Information on alcohol consumption and other variables was obtained through a mailed questionnaire in January 1986.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Information on alcohol consumption and other variables was obtained through a mailed questionnaire in January 1986. Through December 1990, 167 incident endometrial cancer cases occurred in the at-risk cohort of 25,170 women.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The RRs of endometrial cancer associated with < 4.0 and ≥ 4.0 g of alcohol per day compared with abstainers were 0.7 (CI = 0.5-1.1) and 1.0 (CI = 0.7-1.6), respectively.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: These data do not support an association between alcohol and endometrial cancer among postmenopausal women.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: The RRs of endometrial cancer associated with < 4.0 and ≥ 4.0 g of alcohol per day compared with abstainers were 0.7 (CI = 0.5-1.1) and 1.0 (CI = 0.7-1.6), respectively.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Through December 1990, 167 incident endometrial cancer cases occurred in the at-risk cohort of 25,170 women.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Information on alcohol consumption and other variables was obtained through a mailed questionnaire in January 1986.

studies.Reference: Alcohol and endometrial cancer risk in the NIH-AARP diet and health study.
studies.Authors: Yang HP, Gierach GL, Danforth KN, Sherman ME, Park Y, Wentzensen N, Hollenbeck A, Schatzkin A, Brinton LA
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: We prospectively evaluated the association between alcohol intake and incident endometrial cancer in a cohort of 114,414 US women enrolled in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Our results do not support that alcohol is a strong contributor to endometrial cancer risk, but slight risk increases may prevail among some users or for selected tumor characteristics.

studies.Reference: Alcohol consumption and endometrial cancer risk: the multiethnic cohort.
studies.Authors: Setiawan VW, Monroe KR, Goodman MT, Kolonel LN, Pike MC, Henderson BE
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Data on alcohol intake and endometrial cancer risk factors were obtained from the baseline questionnaire.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 41,574 postmenopausal women recruited to the prospective Multiethnic Cohort Study.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Compared to nondrinkers, women consuming ≥2 drinks/day had a multivariate RR of 2.01.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Increased alcohol consumption was associated with increased risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 324 incident invasive endometrial cancer cases were identified.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Data on alcohol intake were obtained from the baseline questionnaire.

studies.Reference: Alcohol consumption, cigarette smoking, and endometrial cancer risk: results from the Netherlands Cohort Study.
studies.Authors: Loerbroks A, Schouten LJ, Goldbohm RA, van den Brandt PA
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: A self-administered questionnaire on dietary habits and other cancer risk factors was completed by 62,573 women.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A self-administered questionnaire on dietary habits and other cancer risk factors was completed by 62,573 women.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The rate ratio (RR) for alcohol users versus non-users was 1.06.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: There is no association between alcohol consumption and endometrial cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Follow-up for cancer was established by record linkage to the Netherlands Cancer Registry.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: A self-administered questionnaire on dietary habits and other cancer risk factors was completed.

studies.Reference: Long-term alcohol intake and risk of endometrial cancer in the Nurses' Health Study, 1980-2010.
studies.Authors: Je Y, De Vivo I, Giovannucci E
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Alcohol intake was measured several times with validated dietary questionnaires.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: We found an inverse association among alcohol drinkers (multivariable RR=0.81; 95% CI: 0.68-0.96) compared with nondrinkers.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: We found an inverse association among alcohol drinkers.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: We identified a total of 794 invasive endometrial adenocarcinoma from 1980 to 2010.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol intake was measured several times with validated dietary questionnaires.

studies.Reference: Alcoholic beverage consumption and the risk of endometrial cancer. Cancer and Steroid Hormone Study Group.
studies.comparison_type: Non-drinkers vs ≥150 grams/week [inverted ⇒ high vs low]
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Participants provided information regarding their alcohol consumption during the preceding five years.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A total of 351 women with primary epithelial endometrial cancer and 2247 women selected from the same geographical areas as the cases were interviewed for the study.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Women who were non-drinkers had a risk of endometrial cancer of 1.83 relative to the risk of women who had consumed an average of 150 grams or more of alcohol per week.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: The increased risk associated with abstinence from alcohol consumption was particularly great in overweight women and was virtually absent in lean women.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol consumption during the preceding five years.

studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.comparison_type: Recent consumption of two or more drinks per day vs abstainers
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Alcohol consumption and other factors were ascertained by telephone interview.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Cases (n = 739) were identified from a statewide tumor registry; controls (n = 2313) were selected randomly.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Compared with abstainers, the multivariable relative risk for recent consumption of two or more drinks per day was 1.27.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: This study suggests that, unlike breast cancer, endometrial cancer is not positively associated with alcohol intake.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: We analyzed data from a population-based case-control study of Wisconsin women to evaluate the relationship of alcohol consumption to endometrial cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol consumption and other factors were ascertained by telephone interview.

studies.Reference: Alcohol and endometrial cancer risk: findings from an Italian case-control study.
studies.Authors: Parazzini F, La Vecchia C, D'Avanzo B, Moroni S, Chatenoud L, Ricci E
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: When total consumption of all alcoholic beverages was considered, 68.2% of cases and 63.9% of controls were drinkers.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Cases were 726 patients... Controls were 2,123 nonhysterectomized patients.

studies.Reference: Reduced risk of endometrial cancer from alcohol drinking in Japanese.
studies.Authors: Hosono S, Matsuo K, Kajiyama H, Hirose K, Suzuki T, Hiraki A, Kawase T, Kidokoro K, Nakanishi T, Hamajima N, Kikkawa F, Tajima K, Tanaka H
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Median consumption of alcohol was only 19.3 g/week among cases who drank and 28.2 g/week among controls who drank.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: We conducted a case-control study with 148 histologically diagnosed incident endometrial cancer cases and 1468 matched non-cancer controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Confounder-adjusted odds ratios for those consuming alcohol at 25-175 g/week compared to non-drinkers were 0.42 (95% CI, 0.23-0.79).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: These results suggest the presence of an inverse association between alcohol drinking and endometrial cancer risk among Japanese women.

extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: Confounder-adjusted odds ratios for those consuming alcohol at 25-175 g/week compared to non-drinkers were 0.42 (95% CI, 0.23-0.79).
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 148 histologically diagnosed incident endometrial cancer cases.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Median consumption of alcohol was only 19.3 g/week among cases who drank and 28.2 g/week among controls who drank.

studies.Reference: Cigarette smoking, alcohol consumption, and endometrial cancer risk: a population-based study in Sweden.
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Alcohol consumption was measured in terms of grams per day.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: We performed a nationwide population-based case-control study among postmenopausal women aged 50-74 years in Sweden, including 709 incident endometrial cancer cases and 3368 controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The multivariate OR for women consuming more than 4 g per day was 0.92.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Alcohol consumption is not materially associated with risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: To assess effects of cigarette smoking and alcohol consumption on the risk of endometrial cancer among postmenopausal women.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol consumption was not clearly associated with risk of endometrial cancer.

studies.Reference: The causal effects of genetically predicted alcohol consumption on endometrial cancer risk from a Mendelian randomization study.
studies.Authors: Yang J, Qu X, Zheng AJ, Jiang F, Chang H, Zhang JR, Yan LJ, Ning P
studies.Stage: Endometrioid Endometrial Cancer (EEC) and Non-Endometrioid Endometrial Cancer (NEC)
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Fifty-seven single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were extracted as instrumental variables for alcohol exposure from the GWAS and Sequencing Consortium of Alcohol and Nicotine GWAS summary data.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: An increase of 1 standard deviation of genetically predicted log-transformed alcoholic drinks per day was associated with a 43% reduction in EC risk [odds ratio (OR) = 0.57].
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Alcohol consumption was a protective factor for EC.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Endometrial cancer (EC) is a common gynecological tumor in females.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol consumption was measured using genetically predicted log-transformed alcoholic drinks per day.

studies.Reference: Alcohol consumption and the risk of new-onset uterine leiomyomas: a nationwide population-based study in 2.5 million Korean women aged 20 to 39 years.
studies.Authors: Kim S, Han K, Choi SY, Yang SY, Choi SH, Yim JY, Kim JJ, Kim MJ
studies.Journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The associations of alcohol consumption, amount drunk per drinking session, and sustained drinking over time with the risk of new-onset uterine leiomyomas were investigated.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Participants comprised 2,512,384 asymptomatic Korean women aged 20 to 39 years.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Women who also reported alcohol consumption in the questionnaire administered 2 years later (sustained drinkers) exhibited a 20% increased risk of new-onset uterine leiomyomas (hazard ratio, 1.20).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Alcohol consumption was associated with an increased incidence of new-onset uterine leiomyomas.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: The diagnosis of uterine leiomyomas required 2 outpatient records within a year or 1 inpatient record of International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes of uterine leiomyomas (D25).
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol consumption was associated with an increased incidence of new-onset uterine leiomyomas of 12% to 16%.

studies.Reference: One-carbon metabolism factors and endometrial cancer risk.
studies.Authors: Liu JJ, Hazra A, Giovannucci E, Hankinson SE, Rosner B, De Vivo I
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Alcohol consumption was assessed as part of dietary intake.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 788 incident endometrial cancer events from 1980 to 2006.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Alcohol consumption of <1 drink a day was significantly protective (hazard ratio: 0.80).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Moderate alcohol intake may protect against developing endometrial cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol consumption of <1 drink a day.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.0996). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 16 studies yielded an effect size of 1.0 (95% CI: 0.86–1.16), indicating no statistically significant association between alcohol and uterine cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 87.18%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
